subject: Data residency + default retention: EU prospect questions
summary: Prospect asks for precise definitions of what we store by default (requests, streaming tokens, prompt derivatives, generated outputs), where EU data lives, and how deletion/exports work. Internal coordination on offering EU-only residency and custom retention follows.
messages:
From: Tara Malik <tara@brightbank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick Q: what do you keep by default (EU prospect)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — BrightBank is interested but our security team needs clarity on a few items before we move forwards. Can you confirm the RedWind (sorry — Redwood) default behaviour for EU-hosted customers specifically:

- Which items are captured by default for hosted/dedicated deployments: full request payload, streaming tokens, intermediate prompts (prompt engineering inputs), and generated outputs?
- Do streaming partial responses get stored, or only final responses?
- What are your default retention windows for these items? Is there a single default or different retention by artifact class?
- If we require EU-only residency and full deletion on request, what is the deletion path and timing? Is there an audit trail proving deletion?

We need succinct answers we can give to procurement/security — ideally in a short bulleted form and a sample log export example.

Appreciate it,
Tara
Senior PM, BrightBank

--
Attachments: none

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Malik <tara@brightbank.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2029 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what do you keep by default (EU prospect)

Hi Tara — thanks for the clear list. Summary below; I also attach a short export sample and our EU residency one-pager. Short answers first, then a little more detail.

Short answers (customer-defaults, hosted/dedicated):
• Default capture: request payloads (full request) and response tokens (final generated output) are captured by default for 30 days.
• Prompt derivatives: system prompts and prompt templates are stored as metadata linked to the request; retention is 90 days by default.
• Streaming partials: we do not persist intermediate streaming chunks by default — only the final assembled response is written unless the customer enables session-level tracing.
• EU residency: for accounts created in our EU region we store data in EU-only storage (Azure/EU or GCP/EU depending on deployment).
• Deletion path: customers can initiate a delete request via Console or API. Typical purge timeframe is up to 72 hours for hot stores and up to 7 days for secondary backups; we record an audit log entry once purge completes.

More context:
- The 30/90 windows are our defaults designed to balance debuggability and privacy. They can be shortened via policy settings or extended under enterprise contracts.
- Prompt derivatives are treated as artifacts because they are used for model routing and cost attributions; we surface them in exports as separate columns.
- For EU-only residency we provide a Data Processing Addendum and can commit to region-bound storage in the contract.
- Audit: we provide deletion receipts (timestamped job IDs) and can produce export samples for security review.

I’m looping in Marissa from Product for confirmations about the backup purge SLA, and CCing security as requested. Let me know if you want a short one-page bulleted doc for Procurement.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-eu-residency-summary.pdf (1 page), sample-log-export.csv (stub)

Thanks Sofia. A few follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm whether request metadata (headers, client IPs) are stored and for how long? We need to know if IPs are logged by default for EU accounts.
2) For the delete receipt, can you share an example of what the audit log entry looks like (timestamp, job id, objects removed)?
3) If we request immediate deletion under our DPA, can you guarantee no copies remain in backup snapshots sooner than 7 days?

We'd also like a sample CSV of a typical log export (schema + a couple of redacted rows).

—BrightBank Sec

Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2029 16:29:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what do you keep by default (EU prospect)

Hi — quick internal notes then answers inline. Michael / Kimberly: please advise if we should include the 365-day backup carve-out in commercial terms for BB-2029-045; procurement asked about deletion guarantees.

Answers to security questions:
• Request metadata: we persist request headers (excluding TLS session secrets) and an anonymized client IP hash for 30 days by default for rate-limiting and fraud detection. Raw client IPs are not stored persistently in EU accounts unless the customer explicitly enables IP logging for legacy reasons.
• Audit/delete receipt: sample entry we provide:
  - job_id: purge-20290118-8342
  - timestamp: 2029-01-18T16:10:12Z
  - scope: bucket://eu-tenant-483/requests/2029/01/10-2029/01/18
  - objects_removed: 482 rows (requests + artifacts)
  - performed_by: tenant_admin_request / api-key
We can redact any internal storage paths for the customer-facing report if desired.
• Backups: our standard hosted backup snapshot retention is 90 days; for EU-only residency we can offer a contract addendum that reduces backup retention to 30 days and commits to a best-effort purge window of 7–14 days for backup artifacts following a deletion request. Fully immediate removal from cold snapshots cannot be strictly guaranteed unless we include a dedicated delete workflow as part of a Reserved-Capacity enterprise agreement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Share the CSV sample (attached) and the one-pager (attached).
2) If BrightBank wants a stricter backup SLA, we can put a 30-day backup retention + 7–14 day purge commitment into the DPA as a paid term. Michael, Kimberly — please confirm feasibility and whether legal can sign off on the 7–14 day language.

Thanks,
Sofia
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
